title: Constrained cell-means models
html:
In the cell-means model of @def-ub-cell-means, let R be a g×p matrix of rank g, and let the columns of the p×(p−g) matrix K form a basis of N(R). Assume that WK has full column rank p−g. The constrained model is 𝛍E(Y)=Wμ with 𝛍Rμ=0.

  1. The constrained model is the full-rank linear model 𝛉E(Y)=WKθ, with 𝛍𝛉μ=Kθ. Every cell mean, including the means of empty cells, is estimable in it. The least squares estimate is 𝛍𝛍μ^R=VRDy¯,VR=K(K⊤DK)−1K⊤,Cov(μ^R)=σ2VR,{#eq-ub-constrained-estimate}

    and its residual sum of squares SSER has n−p+g degrees of freedom.

  2. If every cell is occupied, then VR=D−1−D−1R⊤(RD−1R⊤)−1RD−1, so 𝛍μ^R=y¯−D−1R⊤(RD−1R⊤)−1Ry¯, and SSER−SSE=(Ry¯)⊤(RD−1R⊤)−1Ry¯ is the sum of squares, on g degrees of freedom, of the hypothesis 𝛍Rμ=0 in the unconstrained model.

  3. Under normality, for an ℓ×p matrix L with q=rank(LK)≥1, the F statistic for 𝛍H:Lμ=0 within the constrained model is 𝛍𝛍F=(Lμ^R)⊤(LVRL⊤)−Lμ^RqsR2,sR2=SSERn−p+g,{#eq-ub-constrained-f}

    for any generalized inverse. It has the F(q,n−p+g,γ) distribution with 𝛍𝛍γ=(Lμ)⊤(LVRL⊤)−Lμ/σ2.

  4. Within the constrained model, 𝛍L1μ=0 and 𝛍L2μ=0 are the same hypothesis iff L1K and L2K have the same row space, and then their F statistics coincide.
